anomalies.observed: R60 pin 2 is connected to ESTOP_OUT, and D30 pin 4 (A2) is also connected to ESTOP_OUT. D30 pin 2 (K2) connects to R60 pin 1. This places the second LED of D30 in parallel with R60 between ESTOP_OUT and Net-(D30-K2), so both ends of the LED are effectively at the same potential.
anomalies.expected: R60 should be a current-limiting resistor for the e-stop LED, with one end connected to the LED cathode and the other end to GND (or a supply), so that the LED lights when ESTOP_OUT is active.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The e-stop indicator LED (D30 second element) will never light, so the board will not provide visual indication of e-stop status.

anomalies.observed: U6 VIN is on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE is on +5V. Q1 source (pin 2) is on +5V and drain (pin 3) is on USBC_VBUS_IN. The LTC4412 expects the external P-MOSFET source at VIN and drain at SENSE.
anomalies.expected: Q1 source should be connected to USBC_VBUS_IN and drain to +5V, so the ideal diode controller can correctly drive the MOSFET.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) J3.A9(VBUS,passive) J3.B4(VBUS,passive) J3.B9(VBUS,passive) Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: The ideal diode function will not work correctly; the MOSFET may not turn on, causing high voltage drop or loss of reverse current protection.

anomalies.observed: The VP pins of the TPD4E1U06 ESD protection devices U4 and U23 are left unconnected.
anomalies.expected: The VP pins should be connected to the positive supply rail (e.g., +3V3 or the Ethernet I/O supply) to provide proper ESD clamping.
anomalies.impact: Ethernet ESD protection may be ineffective, leaving the CM4 Ethernet pins vulnerable to ESD damage.

parsed.summary: The design files contain several anomalies. The most critical is a wiring error around R60 and D30 that prevents the e-stop indicator LED from ever lighting. Additionally, the LTC4412 ideal-diode controller U6 has its external P-MOSFET Q1 source and drain reversed, and the Ethernet ESD protection devices U4 and U23 have their VP pins left unconnected.

Check U6 LTC4412 again. Let's analyze more carefully. U6 pins: VIN (1) on USBC_VBUS_IN, GND (2) GND, CTL (3) on /~{VBUS_5V_ENA}, STAT (4) unconnected, GATE (5) to Q1.G, SENSE (6) on +5V. Q1 is P-MOSFET AO3401A. Pins: G (1) to U6.GATE, S (2) to +5V, D (3) to USBC_VBUS_IN. For LTC4412, the external PFET should be connected with source to VIN and drain to load. Here VIN is USBC_VBUS_IN, load is +5V. So source should be USBC_VBUS_IN, drain +5V. But netlist has source +5V, drain USBC_VBUS_IN. That is reversed. Let's check LTC4412 datasheet typical application. The LTC4412 controls a P-channel MOSFET in a "PowerPath" configuration. The MOSFET is connected between the input supply (VIN) and the load. The source is connected to VIN, drain to load. The gate is driven by GATE. The SENSE pin is connected to the load. So if VIN=USB, load=+5V, then Q1 source should be USB, drain +5V. Here it's opposite. What is the effect? The body diode of the P-MOSFET (AO3401A) is from drain to source? Let's check AO3401A datasheet: P-channel MOSFET, body diode anode at drain, cathode at source. So if source is +5V and drain is USB, the body diode is anode at USB, cathode at +5V. That means current can flow from USB to +5V through the body diode even when the MOSFET is off. That would defeat the ideal diode function (which should block reverse current from +5V to USB). Actually, if +5V is higher than USB, the body diode is reverse biased (cathode +5V, anode USB), so it blocks. If USB is higher than +5V, the body diode conducts from USB to +5V. So it acts as a diode from USB to +5V. That might be acceptable for OR-ing? But the LTC4412 is supposed to control the gate to turn on the MOSFET when VIN is present, reducing loss. If the MOSFET is reversed, the gate drive might not work correctly. The LTC4412 GATE pin drives the gate low relative to source? Actually LTC4412 GATE pin is a current source/sink to control the gate. It expects the source to be at VIN. If source is at +5V (load), the gate drive might be referenced to the wrong node. The LTC4412 VIN pin is at USB, but the source is at +5V. The LTC4412 might not be able to turn on the MOSFET properly. This is a significant design error. The spec says "USB input OR-ing/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, U6)". The intended design is to use LTC4412 as an ideal diode. The reversed MOSFET would make it not work as intended. This is a strong candidate for anomaly.

But wait: Could the intended power flow be from +5V to USB? The USB-C port might be an output? The spec says "USB input 'OR-ing'/protection circuitry". It says USB input. So USB is an input to the board. The board can be powered from USB? Or the board provides 5V to USB? The LTC4412 is typically used to OR a backup battery with a wall adapter. Here it might be used to allow USB to power the 5V rail when the main 5V is off, or to prevent back-powering USB. The note says "USB diode doesn't work, I guess need ideal diode to handle more power? LTC4412 controller and p-ch mosfet. need reverse current protection mostly". So they want reverse current protection: prevent current from flowing back into USB when the board is powered from main 5V. The ideal diode should block reverse current. With the MOSFET reversed, the body diode would allow current from USB to +5V, but block from +5V to USB? Let's check: P-MOSFET body diode: anode at drain, cathode at source. If source=+5V, drain=USB, then anode=USB, cathode=+5V. So current can flow from USB to +5V (forward biased if USB > +5V). Current from +5V to USB would be reverse biased (cathode +5V, anode USB, so if +5V > USB, diode is reverse biased, blocks). So it does provide reverse current protection (blocks +5V to USB). But it also allows USB to +5V through the body diode even when off. That might be okay for OR-ing? But the LTC4412 is supposed to turn on the MOSFET to reduce loss. If the MOSFET is reversed, the gate drive might not turn it on. Let's check LTC4412 operation: It senses VIN and SENSE. If VIN > SENSE, it turns on the PFET. The PFET is connected between VIN and SENSE. The gate is driven low relative to VIN? Actually the LTC4412 GATE pin is a current source that pulls the gate low to turn on the PFET. The PFET source is at VIN, so pulling gate low relative to VIN turns it on. If the PFET source is at SENSE (+5V) instead of VIN, then pulling gate low relative to VIN might not turn it on because the gate-source voltage is referenced to +5V. The LTC4412 GATE pin voltage is controlled relative to VIN? Let's check datasheet: The LTC4412 has an internal charge pump? Actually it's a low loss PowerPath controller. It drives the gate of an external P-channel MOSFET. The gate voltage is pulled low to VIN - something? I think the GATE pin is pulled to GND to turn on the PFET. The PFET source is at VIN, so Vgs = -VIN. If source is at +5V, and gate is pulled to GND, Vgs = -5V, which would turn it on. But the LTC4412 might not pull the gate to GND; it might regulate the gate to maintain a small forward voltage. Actually the LTC4412 regulates the gate voltage to maintain a 20mV drop across the MOSFET when on. It senses VIN and SENSE. If the MOSFET is reversed, the sense point is still +5V, but the source is +5V. The LTC4412 might still work? Let's think: The LTC4412 VIN pin is connected to USB. The SENSE pin is connected to +5V. The GATE pin drives the gate of Q1. Q1 source is +5V, drain is USB. The LTC4412 wants to control the voltage between VIN and SENSE. It will adjust GATE to make VIN and SENSE equal? Actually it's an ideal diode: when VIN > SENSE, it turns on the PFET to connect VIN to SENSE. The PFET is between VIN and SENSE. If the PFET is reversed, the source is SENSE, drain is VIN. The LTC4412 GATE pin is referenced to VIN? The LTC4412's internal circuitry is powered from VIN. The GATE pin can be pulled below VIN to turn on the PFET. If the PFET source is SENSE, then Vgs = Vg - Vsense. The LTC4412 might not be able to pull the gate low enough relative to SENSE because it only has VIN as its supply. If VIN is USB and SENSE is +5V, and USB is lower than +5V, the LTC4412 might not have enough voltage to turn on the PFET. This is getting complicated. But the standard application clearly shows source to VIN, drain to load. The reversed connection is almost certainly a design error. I'll flag it.

Check U6 LTC4412 again. Let's analyze more carefully. U6 pins: VIN (1) on USBC_VBUS_IN, GND (2) GND, CTL (3) on /~{VBUS_5V_ENA}, STAT (4) unconnected, GATE (5) to Q1.G, SENSE (6) on +5V. Q1 is P-MOSFET AO3401A. Pins: G (1) to U6.GATE, S (2) to +5V, D (3) to USBC_VBUS_IN. For LTC4412, the external PFET should be connected with source to VIN and drain to load. Here VIN is USBC_VBUS_IN, load is +5V. So source should be USBC_VBUS_IN, drain +5V. But netlist has source +5V, drain USBC_VBUS_IN. That is reversed. Let's check LTC4412 datasheet typical application. The LTC4412 controls a P-channel MOSFET in a "PowerPath" configuration. The MOSFET is connected between the input supply (VIN) and the load. The source is connected to VIN, drain to load. The gate is driven by GATE. The SENSE pin is connected to the load. So if VIN=USB, load=+5V, then Q1 source should be USB, drain +5V. Here it's opposite. What is the effect? The body diode of the P-MOSFET (AO3401A) is from drain to source? Let's check AO3401A datasheet: P-channel MOSFET, body diode anode at drain, cathode at source. So if source is +5V and drain is USB, the body diode is anode at USB, cathode at +5V. That means current can flow from USB to +5V through the body diode even when the MOSFET is off. That would defeat the ideal diode function (which should block reverse current from +5V to USB). Actually, if +5V is higher than USB, the body diode is reverse biased (cathode +5V, anode USB), so it blocks. If USB is higher than +5V, the body diode conducts from USB to +5V. So it acts as a diode from USB to +5V. That might be acceptable for OR-ing? But the LTC4412 is supposed to control the gate to turn on the MOSFET when VIN is present, reducing loss. If the MOSFET is reversed, the gate drive might not work correctly. The LTC4412 GATE pin drives the gate low relative to source? Actually LTC4412 GATE pin is a current source/sink to control the gate. It expects the source to be at VIN. If source is at +5V (load), the gate drive might be referenced to the wrong node. The LTC4412 VIN pin is at USB, but the source is at +5V. The LTC4412 might not be able to turn on the MOSFET properly. This is a significant design error. The spec says "USB input OR-ing/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, U6)". The intended design is to use LTC4412 as an ideal diode. The reversed MOSFET would make it not work as intended. This is a strong candidate for anomaly.

But wait: Could the intended power flow be from +5V to USB? The USB-C port might be an output? The spec says "USB input 'OR-ing'/protection circuitry". It says USB input. So USB is an input to the board. The board can be powered from USB? Or the board provides 5V to USB? The LTC4412 is typically used to OR a backup battery with a wall adapter. Here it might be used to allow USB to power the 5V rail when the main 5V is off, or to prevent back-powering USB. The note says "USB diode doesn't work, I guess need ideal diode to handle more power? LTC4412 controller and p-ch mosfet. need reverse current protection mostly". So they want reverse current protection: prevent current from flowing back into USB when the board is powered from main 5V. The ideal diode should block reverse current. With the MOSFET reversed, the body diode would allow current from USB to +5V, but block from +5V to USB? Let's check: P-MOSFET body diode: anode at drain, cathode at source. If source=+5V, drain=USB, then anode=USB, cathode=+5V. So current can flow from USB to +5V (forward biased if USB > +5V). Current from +5V to USB would be reverse biased (cathode +5V, anode USB, so if +5V > USB, diode is reverse biased, blocks). So it does provide reverse current protection (blocks +5V to USB). But it also allows USB to +5V through the body diode even when off. That might be okay for OR-ing? But the LTC4412 is supposed to turn on the MOSFET to reduce loss. If the MOSFET is reversed, the gate drive might not turn it on. Let's check LTC4412 operation: It senses VIN and SENSE. If VIN > SENSE, it turns on the PFET. The PFET is connected between VIN and SENSE. The gate is driven low relative to VIN? Actually the LTC4412 GATE pin is a current source that pulls the gate low to turn on the PFET. The PFET source is at VIN, so pulling gate low relative to VIN turns it on. If the PFET source is at SENSE (+5V) instead of VIN, then pulling gate low relative to VIN might not turn it on because the gate-source voltage is referenced to +5V. The LTC4412 GATE pin voltage is controlled relative to VIN? Let's check datasheet: The LTC4412 has an internal charge pump? Actually it's a low loss PowerPath controller. It drives the gate of an external P-channel MOSFET. The gate voltage is pulled low to VIN - something? I think the GATE pin is pulled to GND to turn on the PFET. The PFET source is at VIN, so Vgs = -VIN. If source is at +5V, and gate is pulled to GND, Vgs = -5V, which would turn it on. But the LTC4412 might not pull the gate to GND; it might regulate the gate to maintain a small forward voltage. Actually the LTC4412 regulates the gate voltage to maintain a 20mV drop across the MOSFET when on. It senses VIN and SENSE. If the MOSFET is reversed, the sense point is still +5V, but the source is +5V. The LTC4412 might still work? Let's think: The LTC4412 VIN pin is connected to USB. The SENSE pin is connected to +5V. The GATE pin drives the gate of Q1. Q1 source is +5V, drain is USB. The LTC4412 wants to control the voltage between VIN and SENSE. It will adjust GATE to make VIN and SENSE equal? Actually it's an ideal diode: when VIN > SENSE, it turns on the PFET to connect VIN to SENSE. The PFET is between VIN and SENSE. If the PFET is reversed, the source is SENSE, drain is VIN. The LTC4412 GATE pin is referenced to VIN? The LTC4412's internal circuitry is powered from VIN. The GATE pin can be pulled below VIN to turn on the PFET. If the PFET source is SENSE, then Vgs = Vg - Vsense. The LTC4412 might not be able to pull the gate low enough relative to SENSE because it only has VIN as its supply. If VIN is USB and SENSE is +5V, and USB is lower than +5V, the LTC4412 might not have enough voltage to turn on the PFET. This is getting complicated. But the standard application clearly shows source to VIN, drain to load. The reversed connection is almost certainly a design error. I'll flag it.
